verdict.rationale: Aider provides building blocks rather than always-on agents. `--message` runs one instruction and exits, the Python `Coder` API is scriptable, `--auto-test` runs tests after edits, and `--watch-files` responds to `AI!` comments a human adds. Any schedule or autonomous trigger would have to come from external tooling you build yourself (e.g. cron or CI). Community autonomy work ('navigator-mode') is a third-party fork, not first-party. missing for 10: native scheduling/cron or event-trigger agents, persistent always-on background agent mode, autonomous issue/CI-driven maintenance without human prompts, first-party docs or hands-on corroboration of unattended operation.
